transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-22
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Redwood Security), Laura Kim (Meridian CISO), Ryan O'Neal (Cloud Architect), Sanjay Patel (DevOps), Marta Ruiz (Procurement)

Summary: quick security review focused on encryption at rest/in transit and key management options including BYOK/HSM; discussed auditability and SOC2 implications.

Topics: encryption in transit, TLS mutual auth, encryption at rest, envelope encryption, customer-managed keys (CMEK), BYOK workflow, HSM vs cloud KMS, key rotation, audit logs, log retention, SSO/roles for key access.

Transcript:
00:00:03 - Ava Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, um quick roll call, i think we have laura, ryan, sanjay from meridian and then diego and priya from my side. 
00:00:14 - Laura Kim: yeah that's correct, hi all. 
00:00:17 - Diego Ramos: hi, um quick agenda: encryption in transit, encryption at rest and then KMS options BYOK and HSM, and wrap with next steps, cool? 
00:00:27 - Ryan O'Neal: sounds good, we mostly want to confirm that Redwood can meet our BYOK/HSM requirements for regulated PII and financial data, and understand latency impact.
00:00:39 - Ava Chen: perfect, i'll hand to priya to kick off on high-level security posture then diego will go deeper on KMS patterns. 
00:00:46 - Priya Singh: thanks, so from a high level redwood supports TLS 1.2 and 1.3 for in-transit, mutual TLS is available for private deployments, also we can integrate with customer SSO for admin access. we log administrative actions and provide audit trails. 
00:01:03 - Laura Kim: two things right away, 1) we need proof points for SOC2 auditors that keys are customer-controlled for certain workloads, and 2) we need audit logs that show key usage tied back to identity. does redwood provide per-key audit events? 
00:01:18 - Diego Ramos: yes, so we emit key usage events into the audit log, they include request id, principal, timestamp, and operation (encrypt/decrypt/sign). i will caveat that exact field names differ slightly between hosted and private, sometimes the auto transcribed names, but we can map fields for your auditors.
00:01:37 - Laura Kim: okay, and retention? auditors ask for 7 years for some things, is that possible?
00:01:44 - Ava Chen: for Hosted we have default retention windows, but for Private/Dedicated we can pipeline logs to your storage and meet longer retention. we also support exporting to your SIEM.
00:01:55 - Sanjay Patel: just to clarify, on hosted with CMEK or BYOK will the key material ever touch redwood-managed HSMs? we want separation of duties so keys stay siloed.
00:02:07 - Priya Singh: good question. there are two patterns: 1) BYOK with cloud KMS (we request policy-wrapped keys) where keys live in your cloud KMS and we call out for decrypt/encrypt via CMEK APIs; 2) you import keys into a Redwood-managed HSM for dedicated/private deployments — for the latter we can support HSM-backed keys but we recommend a model where customer retains control over key lifecycle via a KMS in their VPC. 
00:02:29 - Ryan O'Neal: can you expand on the BYOK flow? how does Redwood get access to keys to actually encrypt/decrypt tokens at serving time?
00:02:36 - Diego Ramos: sure so typical flow is envelope encryption: your KMS holds the master key (CMK), Redwood holds ephemeral data keys that are encrypted by the CMK. at runtime we call your KMS to unwrap the data key or we use a short-lived cache in memory. for high throughput we do prefix/KV cache so we don't call KMS per-token, the unwrap is infrequent.
00:02:58 - Laura Kim: unwrap calls still show up in logs, right? auditors will want those.
00:03:03 - Diego Ramos: yes, unwrap/decrypt calls are logged on the KMS side and in our service audit logs. those are correlated by request id.
00:03:10 - Ryan O'Neal: what's the latency cost for an unwrap? if we do a synchronous unwrap on first use how much extra tail latency?
00:03:17 - Diego Ramos: rough numbers: cloud KMS unwrapping typically adds ~10-50ms depending on region, HSM-backed calls can be slightly higher, and that cost is amortized because we cache unwrapped data keys for a configurable TTL, default is a few minutes. for high QPS workloads you see negligible per-token impact.
00:03:34 - Sanjay Patel: do you support CloudHSM or external HSMs like Thales?
00:03:38 - Priya Singh: we integrate with major cloud KMSes and their HSM backends (AWS CloudHSM, Google Cloud HSM, Azure Dedicated HSM). for on-prem Thales or Luna HSMs we support an HSM gateway pattern in Private deployments, we can discuss network specifics in the deep dive.
00:03:55 - Laura Kim: and key rotation — can we rotate CMKs without breaking stored artifacts? our legal team requires regular rotation and ability to revoke keys quickly.
00:04:03 - Diego Ramos: yes, envelope encryption lets you rotate master CMKs and rewrap new data keys. we support both rotation in place and rewrap jobs. for immediate revocation you can disable the CMK in your KMS which will make data unreadable until rekeyed — that's expected behavior and auditors understand that. we can also set up a re-encryption job if you want to migrate to a new key proactively.
00:04:24 - Ryan O'Neal: do you offer a bring-your-own-key lifecycle API so our security team can trigger rotations and see key states?
00:04:30 - Ava Chen: yes, for Private and Dedicated we expose admin APIs and RBAC for key operations; for hosted we have a managed workflow and for enterprise customers we can provide restricted admin endpoints or SSO-backed UI roles.
00:04:44 - Marta Ruiz: procurement question — if we want BYOK and HSM, does that affect pricing or change contract terms?
00:04:50 - Ava Chen: typically BYOK doesn't change the base pricing, HSM-backed dedicated options may be part of Dedicated/private pricing due to infrastructure costs; we'll include options in the pricing doc we send.
00:05:00 - Laura Kim: about separation of duties: we need to ensure Redwood ops can't decrypt keys for customer PII. how is access limited?
00:05:07 - Priya Singh: we enforce role-based access, SSO with SAML/SCIM, and customer-managed key policies. For private deployments keys can remain in your VPC-controlled KMS so Redwood staff never have access to the raw key material. For hosted, we offer an option where keys are in your cloud KMS and Redwood never stores plaintext keys. we also have audit logs and can provide SOC2 evidence for privileged access reviews.
00:05:34 - Laura Kim: is there a way for auditors to see a proof that key material hasn't been exfiltrated?
00:05:38 - Diego Ramos: we produce tamper-evident audit logs and can provide hash chains for log batches, and for private deployments you can route logs to your SIEM. we also provide key usage reports that correlate to operational events. auditors usually accept KMS access logs plus our SOC2 report.
00:05:54 - Ryan O'Neal: any caveats on multi-region keys? we have data residency pockets where keys must stay in EU.
00:06:00 - Priya Singh: yes, we support region-scoped CMKs. for hosted we can pin workloads and keys to regions; for private we run the control plane in your region. there is additional configuration for cross-region replication of wrapped keys, but we can keep keys strictly in-region if required.
00:06:16 - Sanjay Patel: ok, operationally, who rotates the keys — our ops or redwood?
00:06:20 - Ava Chen: it's flexible. Customers can own rotation via their KMS and we'll pick up the new keys; alternatively Redwood can schedule rotations in coordination with you. we recommend customer-controlled rotation for regulated environments.
00:06:31 - Laura Kim: one more — network requirements for HSM connectivity, do you need inbound firewall rules?
00:06:36 - Diego Ramos: for cloud KMS no inbound. For on-prem HSM gateway we might require an outbound TLS connection from Redwood to an endpoint in your VPC or a peered network; exact specifics depend on deployment model, but we avoid inbound to your network.
00:06:52 - Marta Ruiz: procurement again — will auditors require us to sign additional attestations for BYOK?
00:06:57 - Ava Chen: usually it's covered by the contract Addendum and the SOC2 report; sometimes customers request a technical attestation we can provide. we'll coordinate legal.
00:07:06 - Laura Kim: can you show an example of the audit log entry?
00:07:09 - Diego Ramos: i have a sample in the deck, i will paste afterwards, but it includes timestamp, request id, principal id, operation, key id and region; note that in-hosted naming sometimes differs in transcription but we will provide canonical schema.
00:07:22 - [00:07:23] - CROSSTALK
00:07:23 - Ryan O'Neal: when you say 'principal' is that mapped to our SSO identity?
00:07:26 - Priya Singh: yes we map principals to SAML/SCIM identities for admin ops; for service calls it's the service principal we provision for your account.
00:07:34 - Laura Kim: ok good. another question on encryption at rest — do you encrypt backups and ephemeral caches? our policy requires encryption everywhere.
00:07:42 - Diego Ramos: yes backups are encrypted with envelope encryption, caches use in-memory keys and disk-backed caches are encrypted. we can provide specifics per component.
00:07:51 - Sanjay Patel: how about KMS throttling — if we have a sudden surge and the KMS rate limits unwraps, does Redwood degrade gracefully?
00:07:58 - Diego Ramos: yes, we have fallback policies: we can increase cache TTL temporarily, fallback to a compatible model variant that uses cached keys, or queue requests with backpressure. for critical low-latency paths we recommend pre-warming keys. we'll simulate in a POC.
00:08:14 - Laura Kim: what about HSM-backed asymmetric signing for audit-level attestations?
00:08:19 - Priya Singh: we support signing operations via HSM for key attestations and can provide signed statements. again location of HSM matters for legal chain-of-custody.
00:08:28 - Ryan O'Neal: Diego, performance notes for HSM versus software KMS?
00:08:32 - Diego Ramos: HSM will add a bit more latency per call but depends on your HSM throughput; for high throughput we recommend data-key caching. Diego: i'll attach a small benchmark doc showing 95th and 99th percentile impacts.
00:08:45 - Laura Kim: okay that helps. on SOC2 scope, we will want the Redwood SOC2 Type II for the hosting environment and attestations around key management.
00:08:53 - Ava Chen: we can share our SOC2 report and control matrix. we'll flag the sections covering key mgmt and access controls.
00:08:59 - Marta Ruiz: procurement wants a timeline for the pilot — we need to know how long to validate the BYOK flow and run auditors.
00:09:05 - Ava Chen: typical pilot is 3-4 weeks: initial integration + ingest a sample dataset + audit checklist. we can compress if needed.
00:09:13 - Laura Kim: ok final thing, will you provide a whitepaper/example config for our security reviewers?
00:09:17 - Diego Ramos: yes we'll share KMS architecture, sample IAM policies, and HSM gateway diagram.
00:09:23 - Ava Chen: great, let's recap next steps: we'll send the architecture doc, Diego will add latency benchmarks, and laura will share compliance artifacts. schedule follow-up deep dive next week.
00:09:34 - Laura Kim: yes that works. thanks everyone.
00:09:36 - Ava Chen: thank you all, we'll follow up by email with docs and calendar invite.

Notes on transcription quality: medium — occasional mislabels, some run-ons, and minor word swaps typical of automatic transcriptions.

References/attachments mentioned: KMS architecture diagram (link sent after call), sample audit log schema (to be provided), SOC2 report (shared via portal).

End of transcript.
